provenance.source: scikit-route 1.0.0a2, skroute.heuristics.NRBS.NRBS at commit 533f320c2f50b57e1ca0858d6c613b475c2884a0 ('Remove dead 2020 artefacts and convert datasets to CSV', the last commit carrying the 1.0 tree; SPEC 4.2: git worktree add /tmp/skroute10 533f320)
provenance.substitution: skroute._utils._utils._cost (Cython 0.29, returns a C float = float32; it does not compile any more) replaced by a pure-Python float64 function with the 1.0 signature _cost(route, length_route, time_costs, fuel_costs, max_time_work, extra_cost, people): sequential sum of fuel_costs[route[i]][route[i+1]] for i < length_route-1, plus fuel_costs[route[0]][route[length_route-1]], times people (1), plus 0 extra trips -- the closed-tour cost in float64, i.e. tests/reference.tour_cost on the label route
provenance.instance: Barcelona (19 places, depot 10000007) built with the 2.0 loader skroute.datasets.load_barcelona() (pairs_to_matrix over barcelona.csv) and converted with skroute.preprocessing.to_dict_of_dicts(bcn.cost, [int(x) for x in bcn.labels]); the dict-of-dicts was handed to the 1.0 code through a JSON dump because the 2.0 core is compiled for CPython 3.13 only (JSON round-trips float64 exactly)
provenance.command: cost, route = NRBS(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5).fit(10000007, ids, cost_dict)  # ids = the 19 labels in matrix row order (the depot first); route is the 1.0 return value: the Hamiltonian cycle read from ids[0] towards its first-attached neighbour, with the start node appended, i.e. a closed route comparable with est.route_
provenance.verification: the 2.0 NRBS(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5).fit(bcn.cost, labels=bcn.labels, depot=bcn.depot) reproduces this sequence and cost; the 446.59 quoted by the proposals is confirmed by this run, not copied
